identity.method: Exact COL26.8 name, author, rank, accepted status, and ITIS source-dataset identity checked against the pinned COL node; each biological source was opened at its taxon account or its paper's explicit Vulpes vulpes treatment.
identity.scope: Nominal species Vulpes vulpes as used in COL26.8. Subspecies and regional populations are not treated as interchangeable with the global species concept.

lifeStatusScope.wild: Claims primarily concern free-living animals; broad range and ecology statements retain the source's geographical and date limits.
lifeStatusScope.domesticated: Fur-farm and captive observations are excluded from claims unless explicitly identified; this record makes no domestication claim.
lifeStatusScope.fossil: Fossil localities and geological ages are kept separate from extant range statements.

sources.title: Madurell-Malapeira, Bartolini Lucenti & Alba. 2021. Middle Pleistocene fox from the Vallparadís Section and the earliest records of the extant red fox. Rivista Italiana di Paleontologia e Stratigrafia 127(1)
sources.locator: Abstract, especially the EVT3 age, dentognathic comparison, and taxonomic conclusion
sources.license: Journal states authors hold copyright without restrictions; no redistribution license declared. Factual claims are paraphrased and linked; article text is not redistributed.
sources.scope: Taxonomic reassessment of described Middle Pleistocene material from one site in northeastern Iberia; paper notes fragmentary remains and taxonomic uncertainty.

sources.title: Carpenter & Mead. 2025. Vulpes vulpes (red fox) remains from Stanton's Cave, Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona. Journal of Cave and Karst Studies 87(4)
sources.license: Copyright National Speleological Society; no reuse license declared. Factual claims are paraphrased and linked; article text and images are not redistributed.
sources.scope: Re-identification of two dentaries from one cave assemblage; authors say this is the first Grand Canyon record and may be the first Arizona fossil record.

sources.version: 2021 assessment; IUCN Red List dataset metadata accessed 2026-09-23
sources.license: IUCN Red List dataset is registered by GBIF under CC BY 4.0; attribution required

sources.title: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. Sierra Nevada Red Fox (Vulpes vulpes necator)
sources.locator: Overview; distinguishes Sierra Nevada distinct population segment from global species
sources.license: U.S. federal government page; no page-specific license statement recorded. Facts paraphrased; no page content or imagery redistributed.
sources.scope: Regional listing for the Sierra Nevada subspecies/population in the United States; does not establish global species status.

claims.text: The 2007 account describes several coat-color forms and external characters; it also reports variation among populations. The historical account's percentages and measurements are deliberately not propagated as current population estimates.
claims.textZh: 2007 年的条目描述了多种毛色型和外部特征，也提及种群间差异。本档案不把该历史条目的比例和测量值当作当前种群估计。
claims.placeTimeScope: Species account synthesis, dated 2007; geographic sampling frame for the reported variation is not stated at claim level.
claims.lifeStatus: wild species account; captive/fur-farm phenotypes not treated as a separate sample

gaps: A current, specimen- and population-scoped morphological synthesis has not been completed.

claims.text: The account reports variable mating arrangements, breeding season shifts by latitude, parental provisioning, and a den-based juvenile period; these are secondary-source summaries, not a range-wide primary-data synthesis.
claims.textZh: 该条目记载交配关系存在变化、繁殖季随纬度而异、亲代会提供食物，幼体有一段洞穴生活期；这些是二手综述，尚非基于全分布区原始数据的综合分析。
claims.placeTimeScope: Geographic variation summarized across an unspecified set of sources; account last updated 2007.
claims.lifeStatus: wild red fox observations; captive/farm data excluded from this claim

gaps: Development, survival, senescence, and variation among regions need primary-study coverage and explicit population scopes.

claims.text: The account lists diverse terrestrial habitats and describes an omnivorous diet, food caching, and possible seed dispersal; these statements do not quantify their frequency or establish global interaction networks.
claims.textZh: 该条目列出多种陆生栖地，并描述杂食、储藏食物和可能的种子传播；这些叙述未量化发生频率，也未建立全球相互作用网络。
claims.locator: Habitat, paragraph 1; Food Habits, paragraph 1; Ecosystem Roles, paragraph 1
claims.placeTimeScope: Educational synthesis last updated 2007; individual study locations are not supplied for each claim.
claims.lifeStatus: wild species account; human-managed landscapes are included as habitat context

gaps: Local diet studies, seasonal variation, species interactions, and urban/rural sampling frames are not yet synthesized.

claims.text: A 2013 range-wide analysis of 729 mitochondrial control-region sequences reported a Holarctic lineage, three Nearctic lineages, and two Japan-restricted lineages, with several inferred to have formed in the Mid/Late Pleistocene. These are locus- and model-dependent phylogeographic results, not a genome-wide species tree.
claims.textZh: 一项 2013 年的广域分析使用 729 条线粒体控制区序列，报告了一个全北界谱系、三个新北界谱系和两个日本特有谱系；研究推断其中若干谱系形成于中/晚更新世。这些结果取决于所用基因位点和模型，不是全基因组物种树。
claims.placeTimeScope: Samples assembled across the Holarctic; 335 bp mitochondrial control-region alignment; Bayesian coalescent estimates calibrated with fossil tips and root priors.
claims.lifeStatus: modern wild samples, with ancient DNA calibration material treated as such

gaps: Genome-wide phylogeny, competing estimates, and later studies have not been systematically reconciled.

claims.text: The ADW account reports native occurrence through northern North America and the Palearctic and introduced populations in Australia and the Falkland Islands; it also assigns both native and introduced labels in part of the Neotropics, so that portion remains unresolved here.
claims.textZh: ADW 条目记载赤狐原生分布于北美北部和古北界，澳大利亚与福克兰群岛有引入种群；该条目也给新热带区部分地区同时标注原生与引入，因此此处保留未决。
claims.locator: Geographic Range, paragraph 1 and biogeographic-region labels
claims.placeTimeScope: Secondary account last updated 2007; no explicit map date or locality-level evidence attached to this summary.
claims.lifeStatus: wild native versus introduced populations distinguished where the source does so

claims.text: A 2013 genetic synthesis used Holarctic sample localities to analyze lineages; its sampling map and sample appendix describe research coverage, not a complete current range polygon.
claims.textZh: 2013 年的遗传学综合研究使用全北界多个采样地点分析谱系；其采样地图和样本附录反映研究覆盖范围，并非当前完整分布区边界。
claims.placeTimeScope: Study sampling localities, including central Siberia and multiple European populations; sample dates and locations are source-specific.

gaps: Current locality-level native, introduced, feral, and captive boundaries have not been reconciled to a dated global range dataset.

claims.text: Dentognathic material from EVT3, Vallparadís Section, northeastern Iberia (about 0.6 Ma) was attributed to extant V. vulpes by comparison with V. alopecoides; the authors identify it as the earliest well-dated European occurrence, while noting the scarcity and taxonomic uncertainty of the material.
claims.textZh: 伊比利亚东北部 Vallparadís 剖面 EVT3（约 0.6 Ma）的牙颌化石，经与 V. alopecoides 比较后被归入现生种 V. vulpes。作者将其视为欧洲年代测定较可靠的最早记录，同时指出材料稀少且分类判断仍有不确定性。
claims.placeTimeScope: EVT3, Vallès-Penedès Basin, northeastern Iberian Peninsula; Middle Pleistocene, ca. 0.6 Ma.
claims.lifeStatus: fossil; distinct from extant range and modern populations

claims.text: Two dentaries (GRCA 76272) from Stanton's Cave were re-identified as red fox rather than gray fox; the authors call this the first Grand Canyon record and say it may be the first Arizona fossil evidence.
claims.textZh: Stanton 洞穴的两件下颌骨（GRCA 76272）经重新鉴定为赤狐而非灰狐；作者称这是大峡谷的首笔记录，并指出它可能也是亚利桑那州首项该种化石证据。
claims.placeTimeScope: Stanton's Cave, Grand Canyon National Park, Arizona; cave assemblage reported as Late Pleistocene and early Holocene, but a more precise age for the fox dentaries is not given in the abstract.

gaps: No global fossil occurrence inventory or systematic reassessment of uncertain historic identifications has been completed.

claims.text: The linked IUCN global assessment is the 2021 record by Hoffmann and Sillero-Zubiri; it must be reported with that assessment year and not represented as a 2026 reassessment.
claims.textZh: 关联的 IUCN 全球评估是 Hoffmann 与 Sillero-Zubiri 于 2021 年发布的记录；引用时须保留该评估年份，不能说成 2026 年重新评估。
claims.lifeStatus: wild populations at global assessment scope

claims.text: The U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service lists the Sierra Nevada distinct population segment of V. v. necator as endangered; this regional subspecies/population listing cannot be generalized to all V. vulpes.
claims.textZh: 美国鱼类及野生动物管理局将 V. v. necator 的内华达山脉独立种群列为濒危；这是区域亚种/种群的列名，不能推广到全部 V. vulpes。
claims.placeTimeScope: Sierra Nevada DPS, California, United States; federal listing in 2021.

gaps: The 2021 global assessment's criteria, trend, threats, and regional assessments have not yet been extracted and compared; status currency needs rechecking before any present-tense global claim.

reasons: All seven facets contain cited facts, but every facet remains partial rather than meeting its full subject checklist.
No reproducible systematic search and screening log has been completed for this taxon.
Global distribution and conservation currency, fossil occurrence coverage, and primary literature for morphology, life history, and ecology remain incomplete.

identity.method: Exact COL26.8 ID, accepted name, authorship, rank, status, and source dataset ID checked in the pinned node. WFO 2026-06 accepted crosswalk row maps the same COL ID to wfo-0000860837 by exact accepted name and authorship.
identity.scope: Ctenium concinnum as represented by COL26.8 usage 3254C. SANBI's regional account and source publication concept are retained as their own scope; name agreement alone does not prove full circumscription equivalence.

lifeStatusScope.wild: Claims come from regional flora accounts; the cited passages do not consistently distinguish native wild plants from naturalised populations.
lifeStatusScope.domesticated: No cultivated or domesticated observations are included; the source does not establish a domestication history.
lifeStatusScope.fossil: No fossil claim is made; fossil occurrence has not been assessed.

sources.title: Moeaha, M.J. 2015. Ctenium Panz. In Fish et al. (eds), Identification guide to the southern African grasses. Strelitzia 36, 182-183; SANBI e-Flora of South Africa record
sources.version: Book account published 2015; e-Flora archive v1.36 issued 2022-06-06; archive accessed 2026-09-23
sources.locator: Ctenium species account, Strelitzia 36: 182-183; source identifier 15446.0; archived Habitat row 80373 and Morphology row 80653
sources.license: SANBI e-Flora archive EML declares CC BY 4.0; source citation marks the item [CC BY]. Attribution required. Only paraphrased facts are recorded here; the individual publication's license version has not been independently inspected.
sources.scope: Regional southern African grass account. The cited habitat statement gives no dated observation sites or population frequency; measurements have no stated sample size in the archived excerpt.

claims.text: Moeaha's species account describes C. concinnum as a tufted perennial 400-700 mm tall, with wiry culms and leaf blades 100-300 mm long by 2-5 mm wide; it also describes the inflorescence and spikelet characters.
claims.textZh: Moeaha 的物种条目将 C. concinnum 描述为丛生多年生草本，高 400–700 mm，茎秆纤细，叶片长 100–300 mm、宽 2–5 mm；条目还描述了花序和小穗特征。
claims.locator: Strelitzia 36 (2015), Ctenium account, pp. 182-183; SANBI/WFO archive Morphology record row 80653, source identifier 15446.0
claims.placeTimeScope: Southern African regional species account published in 2015; the excerpt does not state the measured sample size, life stage, or a collection locality for these measurements.
claims.lifeStatus: Regional flora description; the cited passage does not distinguish wild native plants from naturalised populations.

gaps: Only one regional account has been reviewed; sample size, developmental variation, and independent diagnostic comparisons remain unassessed.

claims.text: The 2015 species account records open grassland and bushveld on sandy or sometimes moist soils as habitat for C. concinnum.
claims.textZh: 2015 年的物种条目记载，C. concinnum 的生境包括沙质或有时较湿润土壤上的开阔草地和灌丛草原。
claims.locator: Strelitzia 36 (2015), Ctenium account, pp. 182-183; SANBI/WFO archive Habitat record row 80373, source identifier 15446.0
claims.placeTimeScope: Southern African regional account published in 2015; no dated observation sites, sampling frame, or population frequency is stated in the excerpt.
claims.lifeStatus: The account does not establish whether each habitat statement concerns native wild or naturalised populations.

gaps: No locality-level observations, seasonality, resource use, species interactions, or population-level evidence has been assessed.

reasons: Only regional morphology and habitat excerpts have been assessed; five required facets remain unassessed and the two assessed facets are partial.
The source population scope and taxonomic circumscription have not been independently compared with all relevant global literature.
No systematic literature search, fossil review, distribution synthesis, conservation assessment, or external expert review has been completed.
